blocks.content: JSON/YAML/XML handling is a core topic in Software Development Fundamentals. It helps engineers build dependable foundations around models, data, APIs, and production services.
This chapter develops JSON/YAML/XML handling from first principles through implementation, tradeoffs, production risks, observability, and interview reasoning. It belongs to the Core Concepts module.

blocks.title: Topic-specific mental model
blocks.content: JSON/YAML/XML handling should be treated as a defined engineering capability inside software engineering for AI systems, with explicit inputs, outputs, constraints, and evidence of correctness.

blocks.title: Boundary rule
blocks.content: Validate data when it crosses a boundary. Never assume a model, library, user, file, tool, or remote service returned a trusted value.

blocks.title: Debugging order
blocks.content: Reproduce the input, verify preprocessing, inspect intermediate state, validate configuration and version, isolate the failing dependency, then compare against a known baseline.

blocks.title: Key takeaways
points: JSON/YAML/XML handling is a system capability, not an isolated API call.
Explicit contracts and evaluation make the implementation trustworthy.
Production quality comes from bounded behavior, observability, and recovery.
